newsitem.title: USA: International Network soars, signals turn in IPOs.
newsitem.headline: International Network soars, signals turn in IPOs.

text.p: The stock of computer network service company International Network Services nearly doubled in its debut Wednesday, jolting the market for inital public offerings out of its summer lethargy.
The stock of the provider of services for company-wide computer networks surged $14.75 to $30.75 in afternoon trade on the Nasdaq stock market.
The stock's rise was seen as sign that some upcoming offerings will receive a warm welcome in the market.

"We're back, and we're back big. We have some good quality deals coming and the 'mad crowd' of momentum players are back and ready to play," said Manish Shah of the publication IPO Maven. "International Network is a very good company with a great future, although it's still not justified at this price," Shah said.
"This company will probably be acquired by another large player, and Cisco (Systems Inc.) is the leading contender becasue of its 8.3 percent stake," he said.
International Network earned $1.7 million on revenues of $44.1 million for the fiscal year ended June 30. For the prior year, it lost $108,000 on revenues of $15.5 million.
It was the first big hit since the IPO market's summer hiatus, which followed a downturn in the broader stock market, coupled with a traditionally slow period.
"It's the best of all worlds from a technical point of view," said Richard Smith, managing syndicate director at Montgomery Securities.

"We've had a terrific flip-flop in the market from pretty negative to pretty positive and a large buildup of cash with eight weeks and nothing to buy. So it's a pretty interesting disequilibrium with a lot of cash looking for something to do," he said.
